html:
Open Collaboration and Target Collaboration are the two ways brands work with creators in the TikTok Shop Affiliate Center, and the difference is who initiates. Open Collaboration sets a public commission that any eligible creator can pick up without approval. Target Collaboration is you inviting specific creators directly, usually with a free sample. Recruit with Target, scale inbound with Open, and run both at once.

Open Collaboration: creators come to you

You set a commission rate on a product and make it available to all eligible creators. Anyone who qualifies can start promoting it without asking. No approvals, no outreach.

  • Pros: passive, scales discovery, zero outreach labor.
  • Cons: you do not choose who promotes, and it only attracts creators if your commission, product, and reviews are compelling.
  • Best when: you already have social proof and want to catch inbound interest at scale.

Open works once your listing is credible. Set a strong commission before you have reviews and little happens, because creators pick products that already look like they convert.

Target Collaboration: you choose the creators

You invite specific creators, typically offering a free sample and sometimes a custom commission. This is direct recruiting.

  • Pros: you pick exactly who represents your product; the way to land proven sellers.
  • Cons: manual, requires outreach and follow-up, does not scale infinitely by hand.
  • Best when: recruiting your first wave and pursuing high-value creators you actually want.

Side by side

Open Collaboration Target Collaboration
Who initiates The creator You (the brand)
Approval None needed You invite directly
Samples Usually not Usually yes
Best for Passive inbound at scale Recruiting specific sellers
Labor Low Higher (outreach)

Run both

The payoff of recruiting the right creators through Target and keeping them active shows up as compounding sales. One seller described the curve: "I joined 3 months ago and went from selling 500 per show to 1000 per show to 2000, and now I'm selling upwards of 5000 to 6000 per show, six days a week" (r/TikTokshop). That comes from committed, repeat collaboration, not one-off Open pickups.

The efficient program uses them together:

  • Target Collaboration to seed and recruit the 15 to 25 category creators you actually want. See creator seeding.
  • Open Collaboration with a competitive commission to catch the additional creators who discover your product once it has traction.

Target builds your core roster; Open captures the long tail. Neither alone is the whole strategy.

The takeaway

Use Target Collaboration to hand-pick and recruit sellers, and Open Collaboration to let momentum bring more creators in. As your program grows, the Target side, the recruiting and follow-up, is where the manual work concentrates and where software or an agency starts earning its keep.

Want your Target recruiting run for you? Book a call, or find the creators worth inviting.
